Exercise A

The Job Ad and the Application

Read the job advertisement and Amy’s application email carefully. Then answer the questions below.

Before you read — optional, not marked
This is just to get you thinking — you can leave it empty and it does not count towards your score.
Text A — Job Advertisement

Receptionist, Waterfront Hotel ⭐⭐⭐⭐

We are offering a job in one of the largest hotels in Melbourne, one of the most amazing cities in the country.

Are you able to:

  • work in a team?
  • deal with guests from different cultures?
  • work efficiently and communicate well?
  • work weekends and holidays?

We require:

  • work experience in customer service.
  • intermediate computer skills.
  • a native speaker or a Certificate in Advanced English.

We offer:

  • a good salary and on-the-job training.

Send your CV and letter of application to Dan Pitt.

Text B — Amy’s Application Email

Dear Mr Pitt,

I would like to apply for the job as receptionist at the Waterfront Hotel. I have one and a half years of work experience in this field. As a student in Cork (Republic of Ireland), I worked part time in a B & B for guests from all over the world, so I am easily able to deal with people from different countries. In my current temporary job in Australia I have six months of experience as a receptionist at the Flying Emu Lodge, where I check in guests and work as part of a small team.

Now I am looking for more permanent work as part of a larger team.

In addition to my work experience I have strong skills in communication, customer service and administration. I also have good computer skills.

I think that I work more efficiently than most people my age because of my experience, and my skills qualify me for this job.

Please find my CV attached. I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours sincerely,
Amy Wynner

Exercise D

Writing: Your Application Email

Imagine you want to apply for a job at a hotel, a restaurant, or a shop in an English-speaking country. Write a short application email (6–8 sentences).

Think about these points

• Which job are you applying for?

• Do you have any experience (work, volunteering, helping at home)?

• Which strengths do you have? (reliable, punctual, good communication skills, self-motivated, work well in a team)

• Why would you be good for this job?

Useful phrases: I would like to apply for... I have experience in... I am able to... I am looking for... I think I would be good at this job because... I look forward to hearing from you.
Your email
Aim for 6–8 sentences. Start with “Dear Sir or Madam” and end with “Yours sincerely” and your name.
